#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Opens the window on a repository, building whatever is out of date first.
#
#   ./window                       this repository's working changes
#   ./window HEAD~1 HEAD           some other pair, as the command line takes them
#   ./window ../redo               another repository
#   ./window ../redo HEAD~1 HEAD   both
#
# The window shells out to dagger, so the tool built here is put on PATH ahead of any
# installed one: a window built from this repository should read with the tool from it.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

# A directory first means another repository; anything else is revisions, the same pair
# dagger itself takes.
repo="."
if [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ -d "$1" ]; then
  repo="$1"
  shift
fi
repo="$(cd "$repo" && pwd)"

reading=()
if [ $# -eq 2 ]; then
  reading=(--before "$1" --after "$2")
elif [ $# -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "name two revisions or none: ./window [<repo>] [<before> <after>]" >&2
  exit 1
fi

port=1420

cargo build --workspace --quiet

# A debug build of the window asks for the page over http, whatever sits in dist, so one
# has to be there to answer. This window starts that server and takes it away again when it
# closes: a server left running is one nobody can see, serving whichever change it happened
# to be started on, to whoever finds the port.
serving() { (exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$port") >/dev/null 2>&1; }

if serving; then
  echo "something is already serving $port — stop it and try again:" >&2
  ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null | grep ":$port " >&2 || lsof -i ":$port" >&2 || true
  exit 1
fi

# The page reads the same pair this window was opened on, so a browser pointed at it shows
# the change being looked at rather than a different one.
(cd ui && DAGGER_BEFORE="${1:-}" DAGGER_AFTER="${2:-}" \
  exec npx --no-install vite --port "$port" --strictPort >/dev/null 2>&1) &
page=$!
trap 'kill "$page" 2>/dev/null; wait "$page" 2>/dev/null' EXIT INT TERM

for _ in $(seq 50); do
  serving && break
  sleep 0.1
done
serving || { echo "the page never came up on $port" >&2; exit 1; }

# The webview and its plumbing come from the dev shell, so the window has to run inside it.
inside="PATH=$PWD/target/debug:\$PATH ./ui/src-tauri/target/debug/dagger-ui --repo '$repo' ${reading[*]}"
if [ -n "${IN_NIX_SHELL:-}" ]; then
  eval "$inside"
else
  nix develop --command bash -c "cd ui/src-tauri && cargo build --quiet && cd ../.. && $inside"
fi

#   ./window ../redo               another repository
#   ./window ../redo HEAD~1 HEAD   both

if [ $# -eq 2 ]; then

cargo build --workspace --quiet

# A debug build of the window asks for the page over http, whatever sits in dist, so one
# has to be there to answer. Somebody already running `npm run dev` gets reused — starting
# a second would only fail on the port — and anything started here is cleaned up on the way
# out rather than left behind holding it.
serving() { (exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$port") >/dev/null 2>&1; }

if ! serving; then
  (cd ui && npx --no-install vite --port "$port" --strictPort >/dev/null 2>&1) &
  page=$!
  trap 'kill "$page" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT

  for _ in $(seq 50); do
    serving && break
    sleep 0.1
  done
  serving || { echo "the page never came up on $port" >&2; exit 1; }
fi

# The webview and its plumbing come from the dev shell, so the window has to run inside it.

  eval "$inside"
else
  nix develop --command bash -c "cd ui/src-tauri && cargo build --quiet && cd ../.. && $inside"
fi

/* The shape of the change: a box for every place code lives, nested as deep as the
 * grouping goes, a node for each definition, and lines for what leans on what.
 *
 * Lines run upwards, because whatever holds something up is drawn above it. A line that has
 * to run the other way is something the reader will be asked to take on faith, so it swings
 * out to the side where it can't be mistaken for the ordinary case.
 *
 * Drawn on a canvas rather than as elements. As elements this was a shape and a name for
 * every definition and a path for every line — some nine hundred things for the engine to
 * lay out, rasterise and hit-test, all of it again at each new size. Chrome has the room to
 * hide that. The webview the window is built on does not: measured on the same picture, ten
 * frames a second as elements against sixty here.
 *
 * What that costs is what a browser gives an element for free — nothing drawn here can be
 * tabbed to or read aloud. The list underneath makes up for it: the same definitions, in
 * reading order, as real buttons that nobody can see.
 *

 * transform itself — moving the view means asking the behaviour to move, so what the reader
 * is doing and what the page wants to show can't end up disagreeing.
